Calendar-time trends with generalised estimating equations

Source: R/desc.R
wgh_gee_trend.Rd

Fits a GEE with child as the cluster (exchangeable correlation) for a continuous or binary outcome on calendar year, optionally interacting with age group, and reports the yearly change (or odds ratio per year) within each age group. The model behind the GEE trend tables of the malnutrition trends study (Ho et al. 2026, medRxiv 2026.07.26.26358982) and the secular trends study (Ho et al. 2026, Sci Rep 16:7515).

Usage

wgh_gee_trend(
  x,
  outcome,
  year = "yearvisit",
  age_group = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  by = "sex",
  corstr = "exchangeable",
  min_events = 10,
  maxit = 25
)

wgh_trend_slopes(object)

Arguments

x

Data.

outcome

Outcome column (numeric or logical).

year

Calendar year column.

age_group

Optional factor column; slopes are reported within each level. Use wgh_age_bands() to create one.

covariates

Extra adjustment terms (character).

by

Optional strata (each fitted separately), usually "sex".

corstr

Working correlation.

min_events

For binary outcomes, age groups (and strata) with fewer events are skipped, because rare outcomes make GEE fail to converge.

maxit

Maximum GEE iterations.

object

A wgh_gee object.

Value

An object of class wgh_gee with the fits and a slopes table.

Examples

# \donttest{
cl <- wgh_classify(growdat)
cl$age_group <- wgh_age_bands(cl$age)
tr <- wgh_gee_trend(cl[cl$age >= 5, ], "obesity", age_group = "age_group", by = "sex")
tr$slopes
